title: Autoscaler signal aliasing caused warm-pool oscillation — findings & remediation runbook
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 we observed repeated short-lived scale-ups across multiple dedicated clusters that led to warm-pool overshoot, higher cost, and P95 latency regressions for inference endpoints. Investigation shows the root cause was 'signal aliasing' between a new readiness probe jitter and KEDA's instantaneous trigger aggregation, which produced false-positive scale signals during transient load spikes. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, immediate mitigations taken, and the action plan and runbook for long-term fixes.
timeline: 2026-02-27 06:12 UTC: Pager alert fired — 3 clusters reported sudden 3x instance increase within 90s and cost ramp on billing dashboard.
2026-02-27 06:25 UTC: On-call began triage; deployed temporary scale policies to cap autoscale-up rate and increased warm-pool retention in affected clusters.
2026-02-27 07:10 UTC: Collected KEDA scaler logs, HPA metrics, readiness probe traces, and warm-pool allocation events for the 06:00–08:00 UTC window.
2026-02-27 09:00 UTC: Initial hypothesis: noisy readiness probe combined with short aggregation windows in KEDA produced repeated trigger firings.
2026-02-27 11:30 UTC: Reproduced signal aliasing in staging by introducing probe jitter; confirmed comparator mismatch between percentiles used by runtime telemetry and KEDA scaler sample window.
2026-02-27 14:00 UTC: Mitigation v1 enacted: increase KEDA trigger smoothing window to 60s and enable 2m hysteresis; revert the new probe rollout to stable implementation.
2026-02-28 09:00 UTC: Observed reduction in scale oscillations; cost spike stabilized but warm-pool retention required tuning to avoid underprovisioning real traffic bursts.
2026-03-01 10:00 UTC: Begin implementation of long-term fixes and automated tests (this ticket).
root_cause: KEDA trigger used an instantaneous sample rate with a short aggregation window while the serving runtime emitted transient readiness probe failures (small jitter introduced in a recent probe change). The combination created aliased high-frequency signals that KEDA interpreted as sustained load, causing repeated scale-ups. Additionally, the warm-pool shrinker was too aggressive, so scale-downs followed immediately and produced oscillation loops.
mitigations: Immediate: Cap scale-up rate via autoscaler annotations to avoid >2x increase per 5 minutes (applied to affected clusters).
Immediate: Reverted the rollout that introduced added probe jitter; rolled back to stable readiness probe implementation.
Short-term: Increase KEDA scaler smoothing window to 60s and enable a 2-minute cooldown/hysteresis for scale decisions.
Short-term: Increase warm-pool minimum size for critical inference pools and slow warm-pool eviction to 10m in Dedicated clusters.
Long-term: Switch KEDA triggers to use a smoothed percentile (p90 over 2m) rather than instantaneous rates for this workload category.
action_items: (A1) Runtime: Remove probe jitter pattern and add exponential backoff to probe failure reporting. Owner: @Ethan Walker. ETA: 2026-03-08. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

(A2) KEDA: Implement configurable percentile smoothing in KEDA scaler adaptor and default to p90-2m for inference routes. Owner: @Marco Diaz. ETA: 2026-03-10. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/keda-adaptor/pull/128
(A3) Autoscaler policy: Add scale-up rate limiter and hysteresis to cluster defaults; expose as runtime config in console. Owner: @Sofia Patel. ETA: 2026-03-12.
(A4) Warm pool: Adjust shrink policy to 10m decay and add cost-aware retention tiers for low-traffic hours. Owner: @Priya Rao. ETA: 2026-03-15.
(A5) Telemetry: Add new metric `keda.trigger_smoothed_rate` and dashboard panels for scale-event causality; create alert if >3 rapid scale-ups in 5m. Owner: @DataInfra Team. ETA: 2026-03-09.
(A6) E2E tests: Add canary tests simulating probe jitter and synthetic spikes to verify smoothing/hysteresis prevents oscillation. Owner: @SRE. ETA: 2026-03-18.
(A7) Post-release review: Run a 48h validation window after runtime + KEDA patches and report regressions to oncall rotation. Owner: @SRE Lead. ETA: 2026-03-22.
validation_plan: After PR merges: deploy to staging with canary traffic pattern that reproduces previous oscillation. Confirm no repeated scale-ups for 90% of runs. Validate cost telemetry for the same window and ensure p95 latency does not regress >5% vs baseline. Run 48h soak in canary cluster then promote to Dedicated clusters in regional rollouts.
notes: We observed two contributing factors: a recent probe change that increased transient failures and a KEDA aggregation choice optimized for very low-latency signals but not robustness to high-frequency jitter.
This incident highlights a recurring trade-off between responsiveness (fast scale-up) and stability (avoiding oscillation). For inference we need stricter hysteresis and percentile-based smoothing.
Cost impact: estimated $28k extra spend over the 12-hour event window across Dedicated clusters; billing alert thresholds will be added to prevent unnoticed spikes.
Related tickets: ENG-116512 (warm-pool eviction tuning), ENG-118001 (probe rollout validation gaps).
